newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Nano urges Berisha to step aside.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Nano urges Berisha to step aside.

text.p: Albanian opposition politician Fatos Nano on Monday joined calls for President Sali Berisha to step aside following weeks of armed unrest in the Balkan country.
In the latest of a series of concessions to the opposition, Berisha on Sunday announced a pardon for Nano, the leader of the Socialist Party who was freed from prison last week.
"I would prefer to shake hands with him as an Albanian citizen and not as president," Nano said of Berisha at his first news conference since his release.
Nano, jailed in 1993 on corruption charges which he denies as politically inspired, was among 51 prisoners with less than two years to serve who were pardoned by presidential decree.
Nano, who was briefly prime minister in 1991, has been mentioned as a possible successor to Berisha, who is under increasing pressure at home and abroad to step down.
Nano threw his support behind the newly-formed national unity government of Prime Minister Bashkim Fino as the best way of returning Albania to normality.
Fino appeared at the news conference at Socialist Party headquarters in central Tirana and greeted his party colleague warmly.
Berisha has said he will resign if his Democratic Party does not win elections due to be held in June.
Nano drew a distinction between demanding that Berisha step aside rather than step down and made clear that he wanted an end to the Berisha presidency through the democratic process.

Nano welcomed the prospect of outside aid for Albania, such as the military and police experts promised by the European Union, but said Albania did not need "Blue Helmets" -- a United Nations intervention force.
He said his party would assist in efforts to persuade the armed rebels to hand in their weapons.
Rebels who control the south of the country are demanding Berisha's resignation, blaming him for allowing dubious savings schemes that failed, bankrupting thousands of families.
The Albanian government is beginning to restore order after weeks of gun law that erupted after angry citizens looted military arsenals.
Sources in Fino's government said Nano had been in hiding since his release from jail and waiting for a pardon before re-emerging in public.

He was released along with all other prisoners apart from those serving life sentences after the justice minister ruled that their security could no longer be guaranteed because of the anarchy sweeping the country.

Nano said 600 other prisoners in the Tirana jail from which he was released had held him a virtual hostage for 20 hours before he was let go because they realised that they would only be freed if he was.
Eventually the prison governor got hold of an ambulance and an armed escort of prison guards and personally drove Nano home.
